rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable type — AI/software developers who already pay for Kagi subscriptions — and explicit willingness-to-pay is on record from the HN thread. The service is highly automatable: a hosted MCP-compatible search proxy wrapping Kagi's API can deliver, bill, and run entirely without per-customer human involvement. The deciding factor is that the gap is real and uncontested — Kagi has no official MCP server — and the technical build is straightforward for Claude-assisted tooling. Operational autonomy meets the build gate floor at 7.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a hosted MCP-compatible web-search proxy that sits between an AI agent and Kagi's search API, translating MCP tool calls into Kagi searches and returning structured results. The factory builds it by writing a Claude-backed MCP server (a small JSON-RPC endpoint), a one-page landing site explaining what it does, a Stripe subscription link ($8-15/mo), and an API-key intake form — no coding by Youval. To sell, the factory drafts targeted posts in HN 'Show HN', the Kagi community Discord, and r/LocalLLaMA, plus cold DMs to GitHub repos that reference Kagi and MCP; outreach goes out only after Youval approves each batch. Once live, customers self-serve signup, get an API key via automated email, and the proxy handles all search delivery; Stripe handles billing; Claude handles support queries from a shared inbox. The only recurring human touch is Youval approving outreach batches and reviewing the monthly Stripe dashboard.
notes: All build_gates pass. Defensibility is low (trivially forkable wrapper), but that does not block build — it just means moving fast matters. Kagi's own API terms should be reviewed before launch.
